title: Ingesting Data (1): Connectors, AMA, Data Collection Rules and Windows Events

header.html: 1. Manage a security operations environment (40 to 45%)

Select data connectors based on data source requirements, including Windows logs and security events; configure collection of Windows Security events by using Windows Security Events via AMA, including data collection rules; plan and configure collection of Windows Security events by using Windows Event Forwarding (WEF)
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

html:
1How data reaches Sentinel

A data connector brings a source into a Log Analytics workspace table. Connectors come from Content hub solutions; you configure them under Microsoft Sentinel > Configuration > Data connectors.

Connector style Examples
Service to service Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Entra ID, Office 365, Azure services
Agent-based (Azure Monitor Agent, AMA) Windows Security Events via AMA, Windows Forwarded Events, Syslog via AMA, CEF via AMA
Diagnostic settings or Azure Policy Azure Activity, Azure resources
API or file Logs Ingestion API, threat intelligence upload, TAXII

The Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) replaces the legacy Log Analytics agent. A data collection rule (DCR) tells AMA what to collect, can filter or transform it, and names the destination workspace.

Need Role
Deploy the agent Virtual Machine Contributor or Azure Connected Machine Resource Administrator
Create or edit DCRs Monitoring Contributor
Configure a connector Read and write on the Sentinel workspace
Exam tip

. AMA + DCR is the modern pattern. Machines outside Azure (on-premises or other clouds) need Azure Arc first, so that AMA can be installed.

2Windows Security Events via AMA

Table: SecurityEvent. On the connector page choose Create data collection rule, select the machines, then choose what to collect on the Collect tab.

Collection choice What it gathers
All events Every Windows security event
Common A standard set for security analysis
Minimal A small set (sign-in and a few key events)
Custom Only the events matched by XPath queries you write
XPath fact Detail
Version AMA supports XPath 1.0 only
Limits Up to 20 expressions per box and 100 boxes per rule
Example Security!*[System[(EventID=4624 or EventID=4625)]] (successful and failed logons)
Validate Get-WinEvent -FilterXPath on a test machine
Exam tip

. Custom = XPath. To collect only logons and logoffs, write an XPath on the Security log with the event IDs; do not collect All events, because that costs more.

3Windows Forwarded Events and WEF

Windows Event Forwarding (WEF) sends events from many source computers to one Windows Event Collector (WEC) server over WinRM. Sentinel then reads the ForwardedEvents log on the collector. This is useful when sources cannot run an agent.

Fact Detail
Connector Windows Forwarded Events via AMA
Install AMA on The WEC machine, not on every source
Prerequisite Windows Event Collection enabled and running on the collector
Table WindowsEvent (not SecurityEvent), even for events forwarded from the Security log
Built-in rules Rules that query SecurityEvent need the Windows Security Events via AMA connector
Subscription type [Windows background] Meaning
Source-initiated Sources are pointed to the collector by Group Policy; scales to many computers
Collector-initiated The collector pulls from a fixed list of sources

Plan the WEC capacity (events per second, disk, one collector per site), the subscriptions (which events), and the DCR (XPath for the forwarded log).

Exam tip

. WEF events land in WindowsEvent. If detections look for SecurityEvent and find nothing, the data is in the wrong table.

4Checking that data arrives

Check Detail
Connector status Connected only when data arrived recently (14 days for policy-managed connectors)
Table query SecurityEvent | take 10 or WindowsEvent | take 10
Health The Data collection health monitoring workbook and the SentinelHealth table

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A company must collect Windows security events from servers in an on-premises datacenter with the Windows Security Events via AMA connector. What must be installed first on the servers?

  • AAzure Arc, so that the Azure Monitor Agent can be installed
  • BThe legacy Log Analytics agent with a workspace key
  • CA Syslog forwarder running rsyslog on a Linux machine
  • DA Logic App that polls the event log every five minutes by schedule
Show the answer

Answer: A. Machines outside Azure need Azure Arc before the AMA connector can be used.

S2A SOC wants only event IDs 4624 and 4625 from the Security log, to reduce cost. Which collection choice should be selected?

  • ACommon, because it contains every sign-in event type
  • BAll events, because filtering is applied by the workspace
  • CCustom, with an XPath query that lists both event IDs
  • DMinimal, because it is limited to two event identifiers
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Custom option collects only the events that match your XPath queries.

S3Security events are forwarded to a WEC server and read by the Windows Forwarded Events connector. In which table do the events land?

  • ASecurityEvent, the table for security log events
  • BSyslog, the table for Linux system events
  • CCommonSecurityLog, the table for CEF events
  • DWindowsEvent, the table for forwarded events
Show the answer

Answer: D. Forwarded events go to WindowsEvent, not SecurityEvent.

S4After deploying Windows Forwarded Events, the built-in analytics rules that query SecurityEvent return nothing. What is the fix that keeps the rules unchanged?

  • AMove the WEC server to the Azure subscription of the workspace
  • BAlso deploy the Windows Security Events via AMA connector
  • CIncrease the DCR transformation limit for the forwarded events
  • DChange the table plan of WindowsEvent to the Basic plan
Show the answer

Answer: B. Built-in rules that query SecurityEvent need the Windows Security Events via AMA connector.

S5An engineer writes a custom XPath query and wants to know which version AMA supports. Which is correct?

  • AXPath 2.0 only, validated with Test-XPath in the portal editor
  • BXPath 3.0 and KQL, validated with the connector page
  • CXPath 1.0 and 2.0, validated with the Azure CLI
  • DXPath 1.0 only, validated with Get-WinEvent -FilterXPath
Show the answer

Answer: D. AMA supports XPath 1.0 only; Get-WinEvent -FilterXPath validates a query.

S6With Windows Event Forwarding, where should the Azure Monitor Agent be installed?

  • AOn the Windows Event Collector server that receives the events
  • BOn every source computer that forwards events to the collector
  • COn the domain controller that holds the PDC emulator role
  • DOn a Linux forwarder that translates the events to Syslog
Show the answer

Answer: A. AMA is installed on the WEC machine, which reads the forwarded events.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which table does Windows Security Events via AMA write to?

Show the answer

SecurityEvent.

R2What does a data collection rule define?

Show the answer

What AMA collects, any transformation, and the destination workspace.

R3What is needed for on-premises machines before AMA?

Show the answer

Azure Arc.

R4Which role creates or edits a DCR?

Show the answer

Monitoring Contributor.

R5What are the limits for custom XPath?

Show the answer

20 expressions per box, 100 boxes per rule.

R6Which collection choices exist besides Custom?

Show the answer

All events, Common and Minimal.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Pattern connector + AMA + DCR; Azure Arc for machines outside Azure
Windows Security Events via AMA table SecurityEvent; All, Common, Minimal, Custom (XPath 1.0)
WEF AMA on the WEC collector; table WindowsEvent
Roles Monitoring Contributor for DCRs; VM Contributor to deploy the agent
Check SecurityEvent or WindowsEvent take 10; data collection health workbook
